We have some code that depends on the Message property that this creates keeping the same format as the original xyz.X.Error.Y strings as originally used by the elog<>, report<>, and commit<> interfaces.

That being said, I'd be OK with a compiler option.

Also, I suppose eventually we should start using the new event format that uses YAML definitions, though the end to end support isn't quite done yet.
Added meson option.

Please don't ifdef error messages 



It only makes the errors harder to add to a registry and hides the need for additional translation of the text.

And each ifdef requires testing each way exponentially increasing the tests required.


we have added parameterized logging to expose such information.
This is message intended to be included in event log message as in line 365.
@mdmii@outlook.com I would need your suggestion here considering the errorName is intended for event logging as in line #365

my point is the message should not have additional components based on an ifdef 

always including the additional elements is ok

defining a new message with additional required arguments is ok

selecting between two at runtime in a ok


consider adding the full object path with the information as context in the additional data.
Are you suggesting changes like in patchset 1?

in that it always formats the message the same way, probably.

I haven't looked where `errorNameBase` is coming from.  If its a registry then no.
constexpr auto errorNameBase = "xyz.openbmc_project.Sensor.Threshold.Error.";

absolutely not, especially without a catch at each caller 


you've created a runtime error that suppresses the useful information that hardware runtime condition was reached being logged and replaced it with reporting information that indicates the software configuration is incomplete, but only when the condition, which is rare and unexpected, is reached.


If needed add a new message.  if the information isn't known to be available conditionally choosing a different message we without the details or using a fixed unknown string is preferable (to me).
